what does he look like? phrase

also look like, what someone looks like, I don’t know what he looks like, what is she like?, describe him

classical

Plaut. Rud. 4.4.111: Quā faciē sunt? (Lewis & Short), s.v. faciēs
Traupman 102: quā sit faciē, nesciō

Quā faciē est?

quā faciē, ablative of quality

The look of a person or thing is an ablative of quality: quā faciē, “of what appearance”; in an indirect question the verb goes into the subjunctive: quā sit faciē, nesciō.

Examples

  • Quā sit faciē, nesciō.

    I don’t know what he looks like.Traupman 102

See also like, face.

SourcesLewis & Short: facies

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 102.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
